name: Australian Standards (AS/NZS 1170, AS 3600, AS 4100)
description: The Australian Standards (alpha 9 track C18), a pack that extends BNBC 2020. Loads: AS/NZS 1170.0 (importance levels IL1-IL4 with their annual probabilities, the ultimate combinations 1.35G, 1.2G + 1.5Q, 1.2G + ψc Q + Wu, 0.9G + Wu, G + ψE Q + Eu and the serviceability ones with ψs, ψl), AS/NZS 1170.1 (imposed actions by occupancy type, the area reduction ψa = 0.3 + 3/√A), AS/NZS 1170.2:2021 (regional speeds VR by region and annual probability, the terrain/height multiplier Mz,cat of TC1-TC4, Md, Ms, Mt, p = 0.6 Vdes² Cfig Cdyn with the wall coefficients), AS 1170.4-2007 (Z of the towns, kp, site classes Ae-Ee with the spectral shape factor Ch(T), μ and Sp of the systems, the equivalent static method V = kp Z Ch(T1) Sp/μ W and the modal spectrum, T1 = 1.25 kt hn^0.75, the drift limit, the earthquake design categories). Concrete: AS 3600:2018 strength design with the capacity reduction factors of Class N bars (φ = 1.24 - 13 kuo/12 within 0.65-0.85, shear 0.75), the stress block α2 = 0.85 - 0.0015 f'c and γ = 0.97 - 0.0025 f'c, the squash load α1 = 1 - 0.003 f'c, beam shear by kv and θv (the simplified method of 8.2.4.3 in the design run, the general method's terms given), Ec, deflection limits, shrinkage steel and the bar sizes N10-N40 (D500N). Steel: AS 4100:2020 members with φ 0.9, the section classification by λe, the member slenderness reduction factor αc with αb, lateral-torsional buckling by αm αs, shear 0.6 fy Aw and the linear interaction. Not covered and taken from BNBC 2020 (named so in the report): concrete torsion, punching, walls, columns' slenderness, the seismic detailing rules, footings, connections, masonry, timber, the bar schedule (BS 8666 as the parent's), the services and every table not in covers. Every value names its clause; VERIFY.md lists them, with the uncertain ones, for checking against the printed standards.
